description: Compute the overall electronic reaction energy of thermal CO oxidation on CeO2(111) via the Mars-van Krevelen mechanism.
user_prompt: Compute the Mars-van Krevelen (MVK) reaction profile of thermal CO oxidation (CO + 1/2 O2 -> CO2) on the CeO2(111) fluorite surface (space group Fm-3m). The MVK mechanism comprises two elementary steps: (i) CO(g) abstracts a surface lattice O to form CO2(g), leaving an oxygen vacancy V_O on the reduced surface (two Ce^4+ are reduced to Ce^3+); (ii) 1/2 O2(g) refills V_O to restore the stoichiometric surface. Report the overall electronic reaction energy delta_E_total (in eV) for CO(g) + 1/2 O2(g) -> CO2(g).

references: Ganduglia-Pirovano, Da Silva & Sauer, Phys. Rev. Lett. 102, 026101 (2009)
method.modeling: Use an O-terminated CeO2(111) fluorite slab with at least 3 O-Ce-O trilayers and vacuum >= 15 Angstrom; remove one topmost surface O to form the V_O intermediate.
method.rationale: Eichler and Hafner report the GGA gas-phase CO oxidation heat of reaction as 3.41 eV, written here in the exothermic reaction-energy convention as delta_E_total = -3.41 eV. For the MVK cycle, delta_E_1 + delta_E_2 must collapse to this same gas-reference value because the CeO2 slab and V_O intermediate cancel over the closed cycle. The CeO2 vacancy references define the recommended DFT+U and Ce3+ localization protocol, but their vacancy energies are not scored when delta_E_total is the final benchmark metric.
